userStories.description:
Design-only. Write the contract into the progress log under ## CONTRACT-001. Do not change production code.

The contract must state:
1. OutputSignals { cli_error: bool, completion_killed: bool, error_text: Option<String>, task_id: Option<String>, run_id: Option<String> } passed to analyze_output. Callers in iteration.rs and slot.rs fill task_id and run_id. No same-typed bool pair at the call. The warn event cannot see fields that are not on this struct.
2. has_cli_error = cli_error || (exit_code != 0 && !completion_killed). Steps 3, 3.5, and 3.6 run only then. When cli_error is set, scan error_text, not output. Otherwise scan output. Step 4 (exit 143 → Crash(RuntimeError)) is unchanged. Not-RateLimit is not done.
3. cli_error is true only for result.is_error or StreamEvent::Error (assistant error, Codex error / turn.failed). tool_result.is_error is ignored. Missing is_error is false. Grok stays cli_error false.
4. RunnerResult also carries a tail-retained copy of the buffer arm_completion_grace scans. drive_stream returns it. conversation is head-capped and is not the fallback.
5. Both paths snapshot the outcome before process_iteration_output / process_slot_result. react_to_outputs reads the snapshot. consumes_budget and wave iteration_consumed follow the snapshot.
6. Sequential order: snapshot, ladder, react_to_completions (wrapper commit) when the claimed task completed, then react_to_outputs. Wave keeps merge deferred.
7. OperatorStopped: Empty + should_stop + operator_stopped → exit 0 "stop signal". StopSpend: set account_quota_stopped, operator_stopped false → exit 0 "quota soft-stop". Keep task_id and output through the ladder. Do not restore 130 or 1.
8. Skip the entire handle_overflow call when the resolved claimed id is in parse_completed_tasks(output). Untagged overflow stays before the pipeline. Git-only and output-scan completions are out of scope.
9. Warn event detection.text_signal_without_cli_error with task_id, classifier, exit_code, completion_killed, run_id when the call site has it. No output text. Correlation id is active_prefix on task-mgr-<prefix>.log.

Downstream: FEAT-001, FEAT-002, FEAT-003, FEAT-004, FEAT-005, FEAT-006, FEAT-007, FEAT-008.

userStories.description:
Move the sequential account reaction out of iteration.rs into orchestrator.rs so a <completed> tag is recorded before any reset, without dropping the wait.

DO:
1. Remove the RateLimit react_to_outputs block from iteration.rs (the block that today returns Empty and drops task_id and output on OperatorStopped / StopSpend). run_iteration returns the RateLimit outcome with task_id and output intact.
2. In orchestrator.rs, snapshot result.outcome before process_iteration_output. Run the ladder. If the ladder completed the claimed task, run react_to_completions (wrapper commit) before the wait.
3. Call react_to_outputs with the snapshot, not the live outcome. record_completion sets Completed; reading that skips the wait.
4. consumes_budget follows the snapshot. A RateLimit snapshot gives the iteration back even when the live outcome is Completed.
5. OperatorStopped after the ladder: Empty, should_stop, operator_stopped true → exit 0 reason "stop signal". StopSpend: set ctx.account_quota_stopped, operator_stopped false → exit 0 "quota soft-stop". Do not restore exit 130 or 1.
6. Tests: E10 sequential — RateLimit plus <completed>X</completed> leaves X done, the wait seam runs, and the iteration is not consumed. Existing OperatorStopped test still expects exit 0 "stop signal". StopSpend test expects account_quota_stopped and exit 0 "quota soft-stop". Inject the wait; do not sleep and do not call the live Usage API (learning 5386).

userStories.description:
Append a limit-shape record so the next real CLI limit shows which stream held the sentence. Do not change which string is_rate_limited, is_prompt_too_long, or is_transient_backend scan.

DO:
1. When exit_code != 0, cli_error is set, or any captured channel matches one of those three classifiers, append one JSON object to .task-mgr/logs/limit-shape-<prefix>.jsonl. A clean exit 0 with no match writes nothing.
2. Each object has provider, exit_code, cli_error, completion_killed, and only that provider's channels. Each text field is the trailing 4096 bytes. Do not put the text on a tracing event.
3. Claude channels: result_is_error, result_text, assistant_error, stderr. Stderr is Stdio::inherit today. Pipe it, tee it to the terminal, and store the tail. result_text is result.result. assistant_error is the StreamEvent::Error string.
4. Grok channels: stderr (the buffer already scanned for auth and transient 5xx) and output_tail (assistant text).
5. Codex channels: error_text (the turn.failed / error string, not derive_output), stderr (the buffer used for the transient check), and output_tail.
6. Tests: one jsonl line per provider has only that provider's keys. A CLAUDE_BINARY stub prints "You've hit your session limit" on stderr and a different sentence in result.result; the line stores each sentence in its own field. The iteration outcome still follows FR-002's scan string, not stderr. A stderr 502 is still TransientBackend and is also recorded.

DO NOT: Retarget the rate-limit scan onto stderr. Do not change Grok or Codex transient classification. Do not log the channel text through tracing. Do not exhaust an account to capture a live limit.
userStories.notes: PRD FR-007. Fixture tests do not prove which live stream carries a limit. This record is the fixture for a later scan change. Learning [5364]: do not narrow patterns. Claude stderr must still be visible on the operator terminal (tee).
userStories.title: Record each provider's limit channels without retargeting the scan
